summary: Kerbside spot on Mabel Street backing onto the sports oval, where other cars already park.
reasons: Oval and trees buffer one side
Cars parked kerbside show it's normal
Nearest buildings are a clubhouse, not houses

best_section.where: along Mabel Street kerb opposite the park access loop, east of the clubhouse driveway

drivers.seclusion: Backs onto a large grassed oval and tree line; buildings across the road look non-residential (clubhouse/shed roofs), with houses set back roughly 60-90m near the park's northern corner.
drivers.access_and_room: Sealed kerb with marked lane and dashed centreline; a white car and a van are already parked along it in the imagery, confirming room to pull off the lane.
drivers.traffic: Through road with painted lane markings; moderate width suggests it carries some through traffic, but not a major arterial.
drivers.convention: Other vehicles are visibly parked kerbside in the same spot in the Esri image, so a van won't stand out.

flags: Road may carry evening through-traffic noise
The sealed loop driveway into the oval could be a maintenance track rather than public parking — don't rely on it
sun_shade: Overhanging park trees to the north shade the kerb through the morning.
cannot_judge: Whether the buildings opposite are occupied dwellings or a clubhouse
